evolution: The early 2000s marked the revolution of ISPs in South Korea. Fierce competition between providers such as KT, Hanaro, Thrunet, and Dacom drove rapid innovation in speed, affordability, and service quality. This rivalry forced companies to upgrade infrastructure quickly, bringing fiber and high-speed DSL to millions of households. Today, major players like KT Corporation, SK Broadband, and LG Uplus continue this competition with fiber and 5G services, ensuring South Korea remains a global leader in internet connectivity.

isps.name: KT (Korea Telecom)
isps.notes:
Formerly state-owned, largest telecom operator.
Launched DSL-based 'HiNet' service in the late 1990s.
Offered nationwide broadband access and became the backbone ISP.

isps.name: Hanaro Telecom
isps.notes:
One of the earliest private ISPs.
Provided DSL and broadband services to homes and businesses.
Focused on offering competitive pricing and faster connections.

isps.name: Thrunet
isps.notes:
Early private broadband provider specializing in DSL.
Targeted urban residential markets.

isps.name: Dacom
isps.notes:
Initially focused on corporate and educational connections.
Offered DSL and leased line services for business clients.

isps.name: KT Corporation (Formerly Korea Telecom - 1981)
isps.notes: The biggest telecom operator and backbone supplier in South Korea. Maintains fiber-optic infrastructure nationwide, offering consumer and business networks.

isps.name: SK Broadband (SKB)
isps.service: Fiber, Cable, IPTV, VoIP, Enterprise Solutions
isps.notes: Owned by SK Group, focuses on urban broadband and high-speed fiber connections. Collaborates with content suppliers for IPTV and streaming services.

isps.name: LG Uplus
isps.notes: Competes with KT and SKB, providing fiber-optic deployment, mobile broadband, and packaged services for residential and business clients.
